  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 836 5393 4664, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 836 5393 4664, Meeting Password: 066081. Members

  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 25, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:03 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Administrative Aide Levi Sinkler

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  METROPOLITAN WATER DISTRICT (MWD) PIPE RELINING  PROJECT ON
  PALOS VERDES DR. EAST
  PRESENTATION BY RUPAM SONI AND JOSE ALDRETE

  Jose Aldrete, MWD Project Manager presented the project scope, schedule, explained
  efforts of community outreach, and discussed opportunities for collaboration.

  Discussion ensued over the need for MWD to work closely with City staff to ensure
  the needs of the community are met throughout the project, including mitigating
  negative impacts on the equestrian community, local schools, traffic and the
  development of the Nature Center.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested clarification on the staging areas that MWD
  was requesting to utilize, as the City has upcoming projects on both corners of Palos
  Verdes Drive East and Palos Verdes Drive North.

  David Wahba, Community Development and Public Works Director responded that
  MWD has shifted its work area, however, it is very narrow. He indicated that MWD will
  need to stage its work outside of the Butcher Park area due to the City moving forward
  with the project.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired about what public relation efforts MWD makes
  to mitigate misplaced frustration with the City and concerns from residents, specifically
  whether MWD intends to reach out to the school district. She suggested that as a
  community gesture, MWD may consider contributing financially to the Butcher Park
  project.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 25, 2021
   Regarding a question from COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA, Mr. Aldrete spoke
  regarding MWD’s bidding process and the requirement that contractors be prequalified
  as the work is highly specialized. He noted that sometime in April of 2022 they will have
  identified a contractor.

  David Wahba, Community Development and Public Works Director discussed project
  oversight by Willldan, including the permit process, traffic control, and the monitoring of
  road deterioration.

  Discussion ensued regarding the project budget and Mr. Aldrete stated the estimated
  budget is $60 million. He indicated that MWD has not yet submitted proposed rates to
  the CPUC and do not know how much they may change due to the project.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN suggested, to the mutual benefit of both the City and
  MWD, that Council form of a two member sub-committee to represent the entire Council
  and discuss concerns while also making the process more efficient.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ nominated MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, COUNCIL
  MEMBER STEGURA volunteered herself for the committee. Without any objection,
  the sub-committee was formed.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ requested to pull item 6E from the Consent Calendar for
separate consideration.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested to pull item 6H from the Consent Calendar for
separate consideration.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 6A-D, 6F- 6G AND 6I
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 6E AND 6H. MOTION CARRIED BY
  COUNCIL CONCENSUS.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS - MAY 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 63934 THROUGH 63979 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $241,123.77 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 050221 THROUGH
  050421 IN THE AMOUNT OF $107,149.23 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $348,273.00 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF MARCH 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF APRIL 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 25, 2021
 ITEM 6E. REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION

E.  BUDGET AMENDMENTS FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021

  APPROVED.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ stated she had pulled the item for the benefit of the public
to explain that staff and Council have a very serious budgeting process starting with a
committee and followed by a public input process. She added that City Manager Grammer
enacted a quarterly budget review in the last fiscal year in response to extraordinary
circumstances around COVID–19.

City Manager Grammer added that although revenue estimates had been very conservative,
with the previous budget process taking place in the early stages of the pandemic, building
activity in the City helped to double what was projected.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN pointed out that the increase is more or less equal to the required
reserves of $1 to $1.5 million and as one time monies to be committed to long term projects
rather than operating expenses.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MAY 11, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 4, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

ITEM 6H. REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION

H.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE AND REGIONAL
  CONTRACT LAW ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF MAY
  13, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF asked if any reports had been prepared on the outcome of the
Peninsula Wide Emergency Preparedness exercise which took place on February 25.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ explained that the City of Rancho Palos Verdes had run
the tabletop exercise for staff and added that it would be beneficial if all the surrounding
cities could do the same type of exercise for staff and elected officials Peninsula wide.

Discussion ensued between Council and staff on the exercise which involved an internal
conversation of how the cities would communicate and respond during different types of
emergencies.

I  RESOLUTION NO. 2476 DESIGNATING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE
  AGREEMENTS RELATED TO RECEIVING GRANT FUNDS FROM THE
  CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 25, 2021
 9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE ITEM RECOMMENDING APPROVAL OF
  RESOLUTION NO. 2475, ADOPTING THE 2021 ENGINEERING AND TRAFFIC
  SURVEY

David Wahba, Community Development and Public Works Director introduced the item and
Joanne Itagaki, Project Manager with Willdan Engineering provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Discussion ensued regarding collision rates and correlation to traffic volume.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ TO
DIRECT STAFF TO APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2475, ADOPTING THE 2021
ENGINEERING AND TRAFFIC SURVEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  TRAFFIC & SAFETY ITEM FOR CITY HALL DRIVEWAY IMPROVEMENTS AT
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH

Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba introduced the item and Joanne
Itagaki, Willdan Engineering, provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA voiced support for the proposed crosswalks.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN requested that the “STOP” pavement marking be repainted by the
county during the installation of the crosswalk.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN
  TO DIRECT STAFF TO CARRY OUT THE IMPROVEMENTS RECOMMENDED BY
  THE TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE AT THE CITY HALL DRIVEWAY AT PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE NORTH, AS SHOWN ON THE ATTACHED EXHIBIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

 City Manager Grammer reported that the COVID-19 case rates continue to go down and
 vaccination rates continue to rise. He stated that in LA County, 61% of those aged 16 years
 and over have received their first vaccine dose. In RHE, 76% of those aged 16 years and
 older have received their first dose and for those over 65 years of age, the rate is almost
 95%. He reported that last Friday the state announced its plans for a full reopening on June
 15 with certain sectors of the economy returning to its usual operations with some limited
 exceptions for events with very large crowds. He stated that Los Angeles County has
 indicated they are going to align with the state's reopening guidelines on June 15 which
 means that capacity limitations and social distancing requirements will be lifted; and, in
 alignment with the CDC guidelines that came out a few weeks ago, after June 15, those who

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 25, 2021
  are fully vaccinated can go without a mask in most indoor settings if they so choose. Cal
 OSHA is going to be meeting next week to vote on COVID-19 work place regulations, which
 RHE City Hall follows and it is expected that those will align closely with the state's reopening
 guidelines. City Manager Grammer stated that he anticipates in-person meetings could
 resume after June 15. He invited Assistant City Manager Davis to provide updates on
 upcoming events.

 Assistant City Manager Davis reported that City staff is proceeding in planning its annual
 events working under the current protocols, however less restrictions as of June 15 are
 anticipated. She noted the postponement until later in fall for the Tracy Austin Tennis
 Tournament, however no date has yet been confirmed. She added that the Mayor's
 breakfast is confirmed for July 10, adding that the Boy Scouts may now be available to
 participate and staff is looking at an opportunity to partner with them. She added that staff
 is considering a grab and go type of breakfast in place of the traditional pancake breakfast.
 She noted that the Hills are Alive event will take place in August and will include both virtual
 events and in person race. She noted that there may be an opportunity for City Celebration
 however there are uncertainties around the parade. Lastly, she reported that staff will be
 going to the Parks & Activities Commission Special meeting next week to propose movie
 nights beginning in June throughout August.

  RECEIVED AND FILED SO ORDERED BY MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

City Council Reports:

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN reported that Regional Contract Law and Peninsula Public Safety
Committee Meetings were held on May 13. The Regional Contract Law Committee
discussed implementing new city seal decals of all Lomita-station contracted cities for Lomita
Sheriff’s vehicles.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  LETTER OF SUPPORT: AB1053

Levi Sinkler, Administrative Aide provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ TO
AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN A LETTER OF SUPPORT FOR
AB 1053 AND HOLD UNTIL THE BILL MOVES TO THE LEGISLATURE IN 2022

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Council items:

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested Council agendize an item concerning a trail riding
business license out of Palos Verdes Estates (PVE) stables which has created noise and
privacy issues for RHE residents.

City Manager Grammer stated that RHE staff is aware of the situation and is currently working
with PVE staff as well as our City Attorney to sort out concerns administratively. He noted that
staff attended last night’s Equestrian Committee meeting to gather input on permitting.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 25, 2021
 Assistant City Manager Davis noted that two issues exist, one of which is the trail riding itself
as well as the issue of where the riders are starting and stopping. She touched on the
Equestrian Committee discussion regarding requiring the business owner to obtain a horse
trainer permit with the business license, setting certain conditions for use of City trails.

Discussion ensued and the decision was made to allow the administrative process to
proceed rather than agendize a future item on a City Council agenda at this time.

14.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS Government Code Section 54957.6
  Agency Designated Representatives: City Manager and Assistant City Manager
  Employee Organization: City of Rolling Hills Estates Employees' Association

15.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:58 P.M. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Diana
McWhorter, dedicated member of the Sheriff’s department administrative staff to the Budget
Study Session on Tuesday, June 8, 2021 at 5:00 p.m. via teleconference; Council recessed
into Closed Session.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Carrie Gallagher, CMC  Steve Zuckerman
Interim City Clerk  Mayor

MAY 25, 2021
